items.fact: The campaign has five chapters and 91 story missions, following Jason and Lucia through Leonida's criminal underworld.
The chapters are Just Like Paradise (Leonida Keys), Paradise Lost (Port Gellhorn), Tits, Ass, Drug Money (Vice City), Vice City, Baby, and Top of the World, Ma.
Chapter 1 has 22 main missions and Chapter 5 is the shortest with 7, while some Chapter 2 and 3 missions are optional (Thrillbillies, Twist Wrist Smash Grab, Kitty Litter Labs).
Chapter 1 centers on Jason, Lucia, Cal, Donnie and Brian, and the opening has Lucia meeting a prison counselor before she is released from Hamlet Correctional.
Chapter 5 involves Giorgio and the ORCAs, Kat and Mattia's baby, a lawyer-arranged deal with Abe, and a raid on Giorgio's penthouse as the final mission.
Leonida is divided into five counties, and collectible cards are spread across all of them.
An interactive map of the game lists 1,075 marked places in nine categories, including robbery targets and hidden packages.
There are 18 collectible card sets (baseball, basketball, football, soccer, dancers, comics and novelty), and collecting three cards in each of the 5 counties unlocks the cards achievement.
Dexerto has pinned 103 collectible cards on its interactive map so far.
There are 33 Underwater Discovery locations, and Kenton's 8 treasure sites (six of which count toward that total) are found with a metal detector and sold to Kenton.
There are 35 WAiNK Curiosities to find, which are small oddities or pieces of infrastructure around Leonida.
There are 27 magazines, books and comics to find (counted separately from Book Swaps), though Dexerto's map lists 30.
Demolition races at Ambrosia Raceway pay over $3,000 on the oval, roughly double on the figure-eight, and can be repeated.
Hunting jobs for Bret in Lummox County start in Chapter 2 (Jason only), and Pilot Pete's timed cocaine air drops open up in Chapter 4.
Large bank vault robberies pay up to $200,000 but only unlock near the end of Chapter 4, after the 'That's Where The Money Is...' side quest and two Payday Loan jobs.
Moses buys untracked stolen cars from Chapter 2 for roughly $1,000 to $5,000 each, while Randy pays $30,000 or more for high-end cars from Chapter 3.
Randy's wish list covers 18 high-end sports cars, and standard-tracker cars can be sold at any Pay 'n' Spray for around $4,000.
Check the WAiNK app for vehicle trackers before boosting a car, since tracked cars can't be sold to Moses.
Cheaper fast travel is available via buses and trains on a schedule, and medium or high-security robberies are much easier with both Jason and Lucia.
In Chapter 4's 'Bad Driver!', killing Felipe pays $20,000 immediately while sparing him unlocks a car later, so save manually first and finish it before 'Power Play'.
Update 01.002.002 (Nov 23, 2026) fixed autosaving, story-blocking phone calls, crashes, weather not changing, and being unable to lose a Wanted level.
Players report a Chapter 3 softlock after the Missing Persons side quest, where Jason is greyed out, and the patch didn't fix it. Loading an older manual save or calling Dunk has worked for some.
The weather-stuck bug persists for many players after the patch, and clearing the PS5 system cache has fixed it for some but not all.
